messages:
maya: Quick mini-sweep results — L4 / T4 / A10G across EU/US/APAC for embeddings + small-chat. Posting raw notes + kernel oddities. Looking for quick sizing recs before we include in the playbook.

jamal: nice, drop the summary table pls. want p50/p95 + tok/sec + $/1M tok estimate. :eyes: 

maya: pasted the quick table below (raw CI run, single-zone, 1k short prompts for small-chat; embeddings use 128B average input):

```
workload    | gpu  | region | p50 ms | p95 ms | tok/s | est $/1M tok
small-chat  | L4   | us     | 62     | 210    | 4200  | $38
small-chat  | T4   | us     | 130    | 430    | 2100  | $22
small-chat  | A10G | us     | 48     | 190    | 5400  | $55
embeddings  | L4   | eu     | 22     | 75     | 9800  | $12
embeddings  | T4   | eu     | 48     | 160    | 5200  | $6
embeddings  | A10G | eu     | 18     | 68     | 11000 | $18
```

li: thanks — curious about kernel choices during the runs. did we use fused-attn on L4? any fallback to im2col? 

maya: L4 used fused attention kernels (v2) for seq<=1024, fallback to generic for 2048 windows. T4 mostly hit the generic attention path; some batched GEMM kernels were thrash-y. A10G used the new matmul+fused attention combo, very stable.

alex: quick note — the T4 p95 jumps correlate with kernel recompile garbage when we hit ephemeral batch shape 1->8. saw spikes in /var/log/kernel-trace.

infra-bot: Deploy report: bench-cluster-eu-03 ran 1.0.4-inferrc with quant flag=INT8 (simulation) at 1719998900.

jamal: were these int8 quant runs or fp16? numbers look mixed.

maya: embeddings were fp16 for parity; small-chat runs included an INT8 sweep (simulated quant) — the cost numbers labeled above account for INT8 CPU-side model packing but runtime used fp16 fallback for some ops on T4. that's why T4 cost efficiency looks better for embeddings but worse for chat latency.

olivia: do we have memory pressure events? particularly on A10G when running 2-concurrent large chat workers?

maya: A10G had ~6% OOM throttles on one EU zone when we packed >2 sessions with 2048-kv. we pinned config to 1 worker per GPU for small-chat in that run.

denise: any regional differences besides raw latency (e.g., kernel versions or driver mismatches)?

maya: yes — APAC nodes were using driver 525.x with cuDNN 8.1, EU/US used 530.x + cuDNN 8.4. APAC showed slightly higher p95 for L4 (roughly +10-15ms) likely due to older kernel path for the fused-attn.

jamal: for sizing recs — if customer needs sub-100ms p95 small-chat in US, recommendation = A10G x1 per ~500 rps (short prompts), L4 can hit it at lower concurrency but watch kernel fallbacks. T4 not recommended for strict latency SLOs.

li: for embeddings-heavy workloads where cost is primary, T4 still wins in eu/us if latency SLO is loose (p95 < 200ms). L4 gives better p50.

alex: ops item — add a kernel-drift check in daily sweep: compare cuDNN/driver across regions and flag if fused-attn unavailable.

maya: noted. also observed quant quality delta: INT8 sim dropped embedding cosine by ~0.7% relative on our eval set; small-chat had occasional tokenization artifacts. we'll run a focused qual eval before recommending INT8 for prod.

olivia: re: cost numbers — are these including infra amortization or raw cloud GPU price?

maya: raw GPU price + estimated runtime overhead (net ~1.15x infra factor). will run a dedicated cost model slide for sales.

denise: can we condense this into a 1-slide cheat sheet (eu/us/apac; L4/T4/A10G; embeddings vs chat; recommended use-case) ?

maya: yes — I'll produce a cheat sheet and drop in #eng-ml once we lock the qual checks. expect short PR by EOD. :thumbsup:

jamal: awesome, thanks. tagging @olivia @li for followups on driver/quant checks.

olivia: ack. I'll grab kernel trace and open a small infra ticket if drivers need updating.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INF-4632 (driver-sync-check) by olivia at 1719999200.

maya: final note — for the playbook blurb: "A10G: best latency; L4: good latency-cost sweet spot; T4: cost-effective for high-volume embeddings when latency can be relaxed." will iterate.

jamal: perfect, this is enough to act on.

maya: thanks all — closing thread after I post the slide.
